name: Ak-Saray and Amir Timur Park
description: The town's centerpiece: the towering ruined portal of Timur's Ak-Saray palace rises over a landscaped park and pedestrian plaza. This is where most guesthouses, tourist cafes, and souvenir stalls cluster, making it the natural base for a short stay. Everything else in town is walkable from here.
pros: Best concentration of guesthouses and cafes
cons: Busiest with tour groups by day

name: Dorut Tilovat and Kok Gumbaz Complex
description: A quieter historic quarter northeast of Ak-Saray, home to the Dorut Tilovat memorial complex, the blue-domed Kok Gumbaz mosque, and the Dorus Saodat crypt. Narrow streets and mahalla (neighborhood) houses surround the monuments, offering a more local, lived-in feel than the main plaza.
cons: Very few cafes or amenities nearby
Signage and information can be sparse

name: Shakhrisabz Bazaar Area
description: The town's working bazaar and surrounding market streets, where locals shop for produce, bread, spices, and household goods. It's a good spot for cheap eats, fresh fruit, and a dose of everyday Uzbek life away from the monument circuit, though it caters far more to residents than tourists.
pros: Central and easy to reach on foot
cons: Not geared toward tourists or remote work

name: Samarkand (base for day trips)
description: Roughly two hours over the Takhtakaracha pass, Samarkand offers reliable wifi, real cafes, more restaurant variety, and better transport links, making it the sensible home base for nomads who want to visit Shakhrisabz without sacrificing work infrastructure. Most travelers day-trip or overnight in Shakhrisabz from here.
bestFor: Remote workers who need reliable infrastructure
pros: Far more dining and lodging variety
Rail and air links to the rest of Uzbekistan
cons: Requires the pass drive to reach Shakhrisabz
Loses the small-town quiet of Shakhrisabz itself
